plan.question: Can a site-specific unsupervised detector reduce nuisance alerts while detecting held-out operational changes without training on attack labels?
plan.experiment: Propose a 6-week offline pilot: compare a statistical baseline with a one-class model on time-separated, de-identified traffic windows. Hold one site out. plan.metrics: Agree an alert-review budget in week 1. Proposed gate: at least 30% fewer nuisance alerts than the baseline at equal detection of the agreed replay scenarios. Report alerts/site/day, detection delay, CPU/RAM, and missed scenarios; simulated detection is not proof of real attack coverage.
plan.companyAsk: Request one engineering contact, a consent and NDA review, a small de-identified traffic export and an appliance for offline benchmarking. Confirm availability before scheduling; do not assume access to every client archive.
plan.researcherAsk: Invite the cited researcher to review the statistical baseline, evaluation protocol and failure analysis; confirm their own contribution to the cited work and current availability. No supervision commitment is assumed.

plan.risks: Normal traffic can already contain attacks; drift may reflect maintenance. Stop if consent or de-identification is inadequate. Test BACnet separately; do not infer BACnet expertise from other protocols.

plan.question: Can a repeatable Gerber/netlist review flag emission hotspots early enough to guide PCB layout changes before external testing?
plan.experiment: Propose a 6-week feasibility pilot: extract layout features, implement a small rule checklist, and compare flagged areas with archived scans. Use leave-one-board-out evaluation and one prospective layout review. Treat the output as engineering triage, not compliance certification.
plan.metrics: Measure hotspot agreement with scans, false flags per board and engineer review time. Proposed gate: identify a plausible hotspot on every held-out failed board, with at most five actionable false flags per review; a small sample gives uncertain estimates. External lab success remains unproven.
plan.companyAsk: Request NDA-protected Gerbers, netlists, stackups, BOMs and scans for the cited boards; ask a layout engineer to annotate known hotspots and reserve one review session per week.
plan.researcherAsk: Invite the cited researcher to help adapt layout rules and explain failure mechanisms; confirm personal contributions, current availability and any rights to existing code before reuse.
plan.milestones: Week 1: NDA, board inventory and annotation rules. Weeks 2–3: parser and baseline checklist. Weeks 4–5: held-out comparisons and one layout review. Week 6: checklist, scripts, evidence log and go/no-go meeting.
plan.risks: A handful of boards cannot establish generalization. Enclosure, cables and operating mode can dominate emissions. Stop if netlists or scan conditions are unavailable; do not promise certification or avoided retest fees.
plan.meeting: A 45-minute meeting with the layout lead and researcher: inspect one failed board and its scan, agree available file formats, select a held-out board and estimate engineering effort.
plan.terms: Agree a capped feasibility fee or joint funding application only after scoping. Keep client designs confidential, separate background methods from new scripts, and negotiate prototype ownership and publication review.

plan.question: Can packaging-film permeability and headspace conditions be tuned to improve raspberry shelf life under the exporter’s actual cold-chain conditions?
plan.experiment: Propose an 8-week pilot: compare the current pack with three candidate films across three independent harvest lots. Log temperature and headspace gases; assess mold, firmness and sensory acceptability on days 0, 7, 9, 12 and 14. Final sample sizes and safety procedures require a food-science review.
plan.metrics: Proposed gate: a candidate meets buyer-agreed mold, firmness and sensory criteria on day 14 in all pilot lots, without unsafe gas conditions. Report lot-level uncertainty and cost per pack. Day 14 is a target to test, never an outcome guaranteed by prior work.
plan.companyAsk: Request sample fruit, current packaging specifications, cold-chain logs and a quality contact. Confirm access to storage and measurements, and cap the sample and consumables budget before the first lot.
plan.researcherAsk: Invite the cited researcher to design film/headspace comparisons and assess microbial-growth assumptions. Confirm personal contribution, lab access and availability; an industrial PhD is a later option requiring consent.
plan.milestones: Weeks 1–2: buyer acceptance criteria, film sourcing and protocol. Weeks 3–6: three staggered lot trials with temperature logging. Week 7: uncertainty and cost analysis. Week 8: packaging recommendation or documented no-go.
plan.risks: Mixed-berry results may not transfer to raspberry-only packs or fluctuating transport temperatures. Anaerobic conditions and sensory rejection can defeat longer shelf life. Do not release experimental packs for sale without the appropriate safety review.
plan.meeting: A 45-minute meeting with the quality manager and researcher: review one rejected shipment, choose acceptance thresholds and harvest windows, and confirm who can measure gases and microbiology.
plan.terms: Propose a capped trial budget, company ownership of shipment records, agreed access to de-identified measurements, negotiated foreground IP and a 60-day publication review. No funding or participation is secured.
